name: woocommerce-mcp
description: WooCommerce (ecommerce channels): me, create_listing, update_listing, end_listing, set_inventory, li

platform_mcp_woocommerce_consumer_key.title: PLATFORM_MCP_WOOCOMMERCE_CONSUMER_KEY
platform_mcp_woocommerce_consumer_key.description: WooCommerce REST API consumer key (WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API > Add key, Read/Write) sent as the HTTP Basic username over HTTPS.

platform_mcp_woocommerce_consumer_secret.title: PLATFORM_MCP_WOOCOMMERCE_CONSUMER_SECRET
platform_mcp_woocommerce_consumer_secret.description: The consumer secret shown once when the key is created; sent as the HTTP Basic password.

platform_mcp_woocommerce_store_host.title: PLATFORM_MCP_WOOCOMMERCE_STORE_HOST
platform_mcp_woocommerce_store_host.description: Host (and any path prefix) of the merchant's WooCommerce store without scheme, e.g. shop.example.com or example.com/shop; every call goes to https://<store_host>/wp-json/wc/v3/... (HTTPS only: Basic auth with the consumer key/secret is documented for HTTPS; plain-HTTP stores need OAuth 1.0a, not supported).

tools.name: me
tools.description: GET /wp-json/wc/v3/system_status (manage_woocommerce capability) returns the store's environment {home_url, site_url, version, wp_version, ...}, database, active_plugins, theme and settings; it verifies the key pair and identifies the store.

tools.name: create_listing
tools.description: POST /wp-json/wc/v3/products creates a simple product: name, type=simple, regular_price (sent as the documented decimal string, e.g. "21.99"), description, sku, stock_quantity and manage_stock=true (so stock_quantity takes effect); the response is the product {id, permalink, status (publish by default), ...}. `currency` is the store's currency (not per product) and `image_urls` need images[{src}] objects, so both are ignored.

tools.name: update_listing
tools.description: PUT /wp-json/wc/v3/products/{id} with only the given fields (name, regular_price as the documented decimal string, description, stock_quantity); stock_quantity only applies when the product has manage_stock on (see set_inventory). Returns the product; `status` is the product status (publish/draft/...).

tools.name: end_listing
tools.description: Unpublishes the product by setting status=draft (reversible; the product keeps its data). DELETE /products/{id} (trash, or force=true to delete permanently) is not used.

tools.name: set_inventory
tools.description: PUT /wp-json/wc/v3/products/{id} {manage_stock: true, stock_quantity} sets product-level stock. `listing_id` (the product id) is required: the endpoint is addressed by id, and a lookup by `sku` (GET /products?sku=) would be a second call the runtime does not chain. Variation stock is per variation (PUT /products/{id}/variations/{vid}, not mapped).

tools.name: list_orders
tools.description: GET /wp-json/wc/v3/orders?page&per_page(max 100)&status(any|pending|processing|on-hold|completed|cancelled|refunded|failed|trash)&after(ISO8601). Returns an array of orders; `total` is a decimal string ("29.35") as WooCommerce returns it; the total count is only in the X-WP-Total header, so `total` of the page is null.

tools.name: mark_shipped
tools.description: PUT /wp-json/wc/v3/orders/{id} {status: completed} (WooCommerce's fulfilled state). Core WooCommerce has no tracking fields: `carrier` and `tracking_number` are NOT recorded (they would need meta_data [{key, value}] objects or the Shipment Tracking extension's wc-shipment-tracking/v3 endpoint, neither expressible here).
